newsitem.title: FRANCE: No new declaration on min wage -French Socialists.
newsitem.headline: No new declaration on min wage -French Socialists.

text.p: Acting French Socialist Party chief Francois Hollande said on Monday that his party had made no declaration this weekend on the scale of the increase it wanted to see for the SMIC national minimum wage.
French newspaper Les Echos said on Monday that the Socialist party wanted a rise of more than four percent in the minimum wage, which currently stands at 6,406.79 francs ($1,090) per month.
Hollande, questioned at a press briefing, neither confirmed nor denied that such a rise was being sought.

He stuck to saying the minimum wage needed a boost but that whatever action was taken should be part of the general aim of improving purchasing power and not just a once-off measure with a limited effect in time.
"There were no declarations this weekend on the SMIC," he said. But I have already said...we want a boost for the SMIC, but we want to avoid it being an isolated step," he said.
"We want a controlled policy of improving French people's purchasing power," he said.
